text:
Predicates:
Pets(x) ::: x is a pet.
ManagedBuilding(x) ::: x is a managed building.
DepositRequired(x) ::: a deposit is required to rent an apartment in a managed building x.
EqualDeposit(x) ::: the security deposit for renting an apartment in a managed building x is equal to one month's rent.
MoreDeposit(x) ::: the security deposit for renting an apartment in a managed building x is more than one month's rent.
Owns(tom, fluffy) ::: Tom owns a pet cat named Fluffy.
Rent(x, y) ::: the monthly rent at building x is $y.
MoveInWith(x, y) ::: Tom is allowed to move in with pet y.
MaxDeposit(x, y) ::: the security deposit for renting an apartment in a managed building x is at most $y.
Premises:
∃x (ManagedBuilding(x) ∧ Pets(y) ∧ AllowedIn(x, y)) ::: Pets are allowed in some managed buildings.
∀x (ManagedBuilding(x) → DepositRequired(x)) ::: A deposit is required to rent an apartment in a managed building.
∀x (DepositRequired(x) → (EqualDeposit(x) ∨ MoreDeposit(x))) ::: The security deposit can be either equal to one month's rent or more.
Pets(fluffy) ∧ Owns(tom, fluffy) ::: Fluffy is Tom's cat. Cats are pets.
ManagedBuilding(oliveGarden) ::: The Olive Garden is a managed building.
Rent(oliveGarden, 2000) ::: The monthly rent at the Olive Garden is $2000.
MoveInWith(tom, fluffy) ↔ (Rent(oliveGarden, 1500) ∧ MaxDeposit(oliveGarden, 1500)) ::: Tom will rent an apartment in a managed building if and only if he is allowed to move in with Fluffy, and the security deposit is no more than $1500.
2000 > 1500 ::: $2000 is more than $1500.
Conclusion:
Rent(oliveGarden, _) ::: Tom will rent an apartment in The Olive Garden.
